title.narrative: Les capacités institutionnelles des organisations de travailleurs sont renforcées

description.narrative:
The Organization of Trade Unions of West Africa (OTUWA) as the voice and visibility of West Africa to ECOWAS and other international labour platforms remains a key social partner for the ILO. To this need with support from the ILO, OTUWA reviewed its Strategic Plan 2016-2020; to assess the extent to which the organization is fulfilling its mandate in the areas on facilitating trade union unity and engagement of national unions in popularising worker-related issues and policies contained in Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) protocols, promotion of decent employment and the elimination of all forms of discrimination, improvement of working and living conditions including the extension and sustenance of social security coverage to everyone and promotion of ratification and effective implementation of International Labour Standards.
In a virtual meeting held in August 2024, attend by 35 members of the OTUWA Governing Council to adopt the recommendations from the Strategic planning review there was consensus on the need to scale up efforts to rebuild and reposition OTUWA. The need for a strengthened Secretariat for effective engagement with ECOWAS and its structures in order for the voices of the working people on issues affecting workers in the sub region on issues such as labour migration, social protection, informality and climate change was highlighted by the General Council.
The strategy of the intervention includes policy advice, training and peer learning. The ILO has several projects on Labour Migration, Child labour and social protection which will be useful for further reinforcement of OTUWA’s capacities to engage with ECOWAS.
